extracted.intended_audience: general readers and people interested in public relations or journalism (e.g., PR practitioners, journalism students)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and normative guidance about what a press release (新聞稿/通訊稿) is, how it is used, distributed, and how it differs from related forms (e.g., communiqués, advertorials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a press release (新聞稿 / 通訊稿)
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release (新聞稿), also called a 通訊稿, is a news-style publicity document sent by companies, institutions, governments, schools, etc., to news media to announce information that has news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states the press release is '一種新聞式宣傳文稿，由公司、機構、政府、學校等單位發送予新聞媒體的通信文件，用以公佈有新聞價值的消息。' It also notes that when issued by government departments or after meetings of international leaders, such releases are called '公報' (communiqué).

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are intended to announce messages that possess news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit phrasing: '用以公佈有新聞價值的消息.' This implies that material lacking news value is not proper subject matter for a conventional press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution channels and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Common means of distributing press releases include official websites, email, fax, and printed (computer-printed) letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists distribution methods: '上網、官方網頁、電子郵件、傳真、書信（電腦打印）形式分發' and notes recipients include newspapers, magazines, radio, television (networks), and news agencies. It also notes that commercial distribution services exist to disseminate business press releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended recipients and target outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are directed to editors of newspapers, magazines, radio and TV stations, and news agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article emphasizes the release is sent to media editors and that professional distribution services can target these outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to journalist-produced news (authorship and editorial control)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases are produced by organizations for media; they are not the same as news articles written by journalists for news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes publishers/senders do not mind whether newsrooms publish the release verbatim, but journalists are free to edit the material and write news stories based on it ('發布者不介意新聞社是否原稿照登，不過新聞記者可編輯題材、撰寫成新聞稿件'). It warns that releases from organizations should not be conflated with journalist-authored copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use to announce press conferences or events
rubrics_metrics.description: A common function of press releases is to notify media about upcoming press conferences or events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states '不少新聞稿是通知各大傳媒有關記者招待會的消息.' This suggests timing and event-notification are typical press-release purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology distinction in Chinese context (新聞稿 vs 通訊稿)
rubrics_metrics.description: In Chinese usage, 通訊稿 and 新聞稿 are often synonymous, but 通訊稿 typically emphasizes reporting on the process of events or meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article explains: '雖然在中文語境上，通訊稿與新聞稿同義，但通常偏重於活動或會議過程.' This is a stylistic/genre distinction useful when producing releases for Chinese-language media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid advertorials and disguised promotional pieces (鱔稿 / 業配新聞 / 廣編稿)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes advertisers pay publishers to run promotional copy resembling news; these paid items are called different names regionally and are distinct from independent news coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article identifies the phenomenon: in Hong Kong called '鱔稿', in Taiwan '業配新聞' or '廣編稿', noting that advertisers may pay publishers to publish such material to achieve promotional effect. This serves as a caution about paid vs. editorially independent press content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official/government communications labeled as communiqués (公報 / communiqué)
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases issued by government bodies or after international leader meetings may be referred to as communiqués (公報 / communiqué).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entry clarifies terminology and formal usage for governmental statements: '由政府部門發布、或國際領袖會面後發布的新聞稿，又稱為「公報」(communiqué)'. This signals a higher-formality subtype of press release.
